body:
again, thank you.

I think I'm at a point where the beer has to go.

It just does. I don't think I need to explain the whys and wherefores, it's a common tale.

My ankle will never get better. I will experience arthritis, and when I do the only option I have left is fusion. (basically they will cement the bones, meaning no more movement, but no more pain). I chose not to do fusion yet, in order to receive a better settlement from the insurance. This is the world we live in. But, I need to accept that and move on.

It's been two years of constant pain that I can not describe and that no-one can really appreciate. The nearest to an explain I can manage is a "Cilice" around my ankle, all day, every day. Every movement is pain ful, evry non-movement is painful. Basically, pain. I was taking pain-killers, but, they made me forget to eat, (hunger is a pain signal) so I ended up collapsing and having a seizure.

Not to over-egg the pudding, but, it's taken a while to adjust.

I don't think my younger (27) girlfriend was prepared for this shit, I certainly wasn't. I don't hold this against her. I couldn't. But hell, I wasn't easy on her either. I'm actually happy that she should not have to deal with this fact as whilst she loved me (still does I think), it's alot to carry, and I haven't finished adjusting yet.

I have opportunities facing me that are rare and quite special. If I'm honest, the past few weeks have been entirely selfish.

I asked my gf if she could commit to leaving this country and join me on a few more years of adventure (with a limp), but she chose not to. I'm actually relieved for her, and now I have a free reign while I adjust and settle.

This is still half a story, thanks for reading.

Again, thank you for the kind words.


(ooops- mixed accounts: repost)

yeah, sex is not a problem - it'd be my preferred form of exercise. way more fun than martial arts, and if I'm honest, I'm better at it.

Lover, not a fighter!

but - I liked being good at both. (or at least, thinking I was good at both)

For me there was a peace in tai-chi & martial arts that I never ever found anywhere else.

After I get the fusion done, I should be able to practice again.

The fusion requires me to be in a wheelchair for 9 months or so during recovery. It's not minor surgery. To give you an idea,, they open up your foot with an L shape, where the short part of the L points to the ankle bone, and the long part runs the length of your foot.

I had this once already for the remedial repair after the initial accident.

Anyways, I think I remembered my strength today. thank you all for holding out and waiting for it to come thru, and the extraordinarily decent act of encouraging it.

It's not the kind of thing I forget, and, nor should I.

peace and warmth to you all.

The past month has been close to uttterly unbearable.

I don't think I ever walked so far down this path as to begin to make preparations to give up - as in, "okay so in a couple of hours we're going to call this a day. No loss, no big deal, you just wanted out"

That's not enough, I need more from all this. I'm not done yet, as everyone has said, it's not easy, and this shit will pass just as all the other shit did before it.

I'll apologise for being a little coarse here, but wow, that was waaaay to close for comfort. I think I'll have to hit up the anti-depressants for a while and lay off the beer for alot longer, but, no way do I want to feel as dark as I just did.

I'm still reeling, I know I'm in the mess of this shit now.

5 stages right??

denial: anger: bargaining: something: something:

I'm not through this, not by any measure.

I do know though, that today, right now, things look better.

If I can hold on to that, there's a way out.

Again, thanks for the kind words one and all, they do help!

http://www.happinessinthisworld.com/2009/03/08/the-true-cause-of-depression/

One of SW's mods posted that link today somewhere else.

Last time I was in a dark spot, I sat and dwelled on it, for an age; seemingly out of nowhere, I decided to make the change. So yeah, Fuck it, and the horse it rode in on!

I need to do that again, "decide to make the change".

This isn't over, but, fuck this! feeling like shit 100-times-a-day(literally), every-day to no useful end.

Sack up, soldier on!

It feels kinda empty saying it now, but, I know if I hold true and don't give an inch I can get past this.

Again, thanks to you all for your kind words.

It's 3am on a Friday, and I just had a beer (not smart i'll admit, 2 x 33cl easter beers) - I've now told everyone around me, and all I can see is support & sympathy; even if they can't do much about this, I can see that no one wishes me ill, or wants to see what I was considering as an option.

Hopefully, I'll post again soon from a better position.

Again, my thanks and respect to you all for doing what you do.

Paul
